newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SNS says reduce Dutch financials overweighting.
newsitem.headline: SNS says reduce Dutch financials overweighting.

text.p: SNS Securities said on Tuesday investors should reduce overweight positions in Dutch financial stocks after first half results due over the next two weeks.

The broker said Dutch financials had performed excellently as a result of a restructuring of the Dutch banking market in the early 1990s, release of loan loss provisions, disclosure of results under U.S. GAAP rules, booming financial markets, the higher dollar and lower interest rates.
"The grand question remains whether investors should still be overweighted in financials," SNS said in a research note from analyst Nico van Geest.
"Our opinion is (to reduce the) overweighting in the second half of 1997 after the release of the first half 1997 results," it added.
"Dividend yields are below money market rates and price/book values above 2.0 of banks are rather high."
SNS said it had downgraded bank ABN AMRO to a Hold, or a rating of 3, from a Buy, or rating 2, in June.
It said Aegon was a selected-list stock with a rating of 1 as it had underperformed other financials and was the least interest rate-sensitive stock, while all others had a rating of 2.
"We might lower ratings after the release of the first half results," SNS said.
The other stocks covered by the research note were ING Groep, ASR Holding, NIB and Fortis Amev
